title: Facet lattice and supported-series coordinate cover of a complete toric model
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid, written additively, whose only invertible element is $0$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Put $G=P^{m gp}$. Let $n\ge0$. For a local coefficient ring $L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be the completion of $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q
e0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Consider either a field $L=k$ with $R=B_k(P,n)$, or a Cohen ring $L=C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with $R=B_C(P,n)/(	heta)$, where $	heta-p\in(z^q\ (q
e0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In either case $z^q$ denotes the image of the chart monomial in $R$. Assume $R$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $\sigma\subset G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ be the cone generated by $P$, let $\mathcal F$ be its set of facets, and let $
u_F:G	o\mathbf Z$ be their primitive nonnegative forms [def-trf-sharp-monoid-facet-forms]. Then $\mathcal F$ is finite; writing $r=|\mathcal F|$ and choosing an enumeration, the homomorphism $
u=(
u_F)_F:G	o\mathbf Z^r$ is injective. With $M=
u(G)$, one has $
u(P)=M\cap\mathbf N^r$. If $P
e\{0\}$, there is $c\in P$ for which every coordinate of $w=
u(c)$ is strictly positive. Put $B=B_L(P,n)$ and $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The homomorphism on polynomials $z^qt^a\mapsto X^{
u(q)}t^a$ extends to an injective $L$-algebra map $\iota:B	o A$ whose image is exactly the series supported on $(M\cap\mathbf N^r)	imes\mathbf N^n$. Deleting all other coefficients gives a $B$-linear retraction $ho:A	o B$ with $ho\iota=1_B$. In the field case set $D=A$ and $ arho=ho$. In the Cohen case put $\Theta=\iota(	heta)$ and $D=A/(\Theta)$; then $B\cap\Theta A=	heta B$ under $\iota$, and $ arho([a])=[ho(a)]$ is well defined. In both cases the induced map $R	o D$ is injective, $ arho:D	o R$ is $R$-linear and restricts to the identity on $R$, and, writing $X^v$ for the image in $D$ of a coordinate monomial, $ arho(X^v)=0$ for $v\in\mathbf N^r\setminus M$, while $ arho(X^{
u(q)})=z^q$ for every $q\in P$. These assertions include $P=\{0\}$, $r=0$ and $n=0$, except that the strictly positive vector is asserted only for $P
e\{0\}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharp-cone-primitive-facet-preparation] to $P$: its finite generation, integrality, saturation and sharpness are exactly our assumptions. It gives a finite facet set, the primitive normals, the embedding $G\subset V=G\otimes\mathbf Q$, pointedness of $\sigma$, $P=\sigma\cap G$, and $\sigma=\{x:\nu_F(x)\ge0\ (F\in\mathcal F)\}$. These normals are those in the statement, since [def-trf-sharp-monoid-facet-forms] identifies primitive facet forms with primitive facet normals and the preparation lemma gives uniqueness.

proof.text:
If $
u(g)=0$, the facet inequalities put both $g$ and $-g$ in $\sigma$; pointedness and $G\subset V$ give $g=0$. Thus $
u$ is injective. For $
u(g)\in\mathbf N^r$ the same inequalities give $g\in\sigma\cap G=P$; the converse is nonnegativity of the forms. Hence $
u(P)=M\cap\mathbf N^r$. These are direct consequences of the statements supplied in step 1.

proof.text:
If $P
e\{0\}$, choose finite monoid generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ and put $c=\sum_j a_j$. For each facet $F$, at least one $
u_F(a_j)$ is positive: otherwise $
u_F$ vanishes on all generators of $P$, hence on their differences, which generate $G$, contrary to its surjectivity. All these values are nonnegative integers, so $
u_F(c)>0$ for every $F$. This proves the asserted positivity without choosing unrelated facet witnesses.

proof.text: Put $M'=M\times\mathbf Z^n\subset\mathbf Z^{r+n}$ and $Q'=M'\cap\mathbf N^{r+n}=(M\cap\mathbf N^r)\times\mathbf N^n$. The map $(q,a)\mapsto(\nu(q),a)$ is a monoid isomorphism $P\times\mathbf N^n\simeq Q'$; it induces the polynomial-ring isomorphism $L[P][t]\simeq L[Q']$ by the displayed monomial formula. Nonzero pairs correspond to nonzero exponents. Their monomial ideal is exactly $(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$: each nonconstant monomial has a nonzero $P$-part or is divisible by a $t_j$. Thus the isomorphism identifies the completion ideals and their powers, and induces inverse isomorphisms on all quotients and on their compatible sequences. In particular $B$ is the completion used in [lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection] for $Q'$. This $Q'$ is finitely generated by the images of generators of $P$ and the $n$ coordinate vectors. For a field $L$ its maximal ideal is zero (finitely generated), and its zero-adic completion is $L$. For a Cohen ring these hypotheses hold because its maximal ideal is $(p)$ and it is complete, by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. The support-projection lemma therefore gives $\iota:B\hookrightarrow A$ with exactly the asserted support and monomial formula, and the $B$-linear coefficient-deletion retraction $\rho$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the facet-lattice and supported-series argument; ILO Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies model notation only.

proof.text: In the Cohen case identify $B$ with its image under $\iota$ and put $\Theta=\iota(\theta)$. If $\iota(b)=\Theta a$, apply $\rho$: $b=\rho(\Theta a)=\theta\rho(a)$. Conversely $\iota(\theta b)=\Theta\iota(b)$. Thus $B\cap\Theta A=\theta B$, and if $\iota(b)$ becomes zero modulo $\Theta$, then $b$ is zero modulo $\theta$; the induced ring map $R\to D$ is injective. If $a'-a=\Theta h$, then $\rho(a')-\rho(a)=\theta\rho(h)$, so $\bar\rho([a])=[\rho(a)]$ is independent of the representative. For $b\in B$, $\bar\rho([\iota(b)a])=[b\rho(a)]$ and $\bar\rho([\iota(b)])=[b]$ by $B$-linearity and $\rho\iota=1$. These equations also show independence of the representative of $[b]\in R$, and prove $R$-linearity and the retraction property. The field case is directly $R=B$, $D=A$, $\bar\rho=\rho$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the facet-lattice and supported-series argument; ILO Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies model notation only.

proof.text: The support projection of step 4 deletes $X^v$ when $v\notin M$, since its full exponent $(v,0)$ lies outside $Q'$, and fixes $X^{\nu(q)}=\iota(z^q)$. Passing to the quotients in step 5 gives the two required formulas for $\bar\rho$. For $P=\{0\}$ the preparation lemma in step 1 gives $G=0$ and no facets; $M'=\mathbf Z^n$, $Q'=\mathbf N^n$, so step 4 is the identity power-series presentation and its projection is the identity. When $n=0$ there are simply no $t$ coordinates in the same argument, including $P=\{0\}$ where $A=L$. No step used the normal-domain hypothesis or the congruence on $\theta$; retaining them as assumed causes no problem, and the quotient calculation holds for every $\theta\in B$.
